name: Marlborough

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: Marlborough is by far New Zealand's largest wine region, with three quarters of the country's wine production and 70% of its vineyard area in 2020.
Marlborough was registered as a Geographical Indication in 2018, and it is most famous for its acclaimed style of Sauvignon Blanc.
Central Wairau Valley soils are free-draining gravels and stony riverbeds, and cooling sea breezes and cool nights give a strong day to night temperature swing.
The three subregions are the Wairau Valley, the Southern Valleys with older soils richer in clay, and the cooler Awatere Valley.
Méthode Marlborough wines must be made entirely in Marlborough by the traditional method and aged on lees for a minimum of 18 months.
Appellation Marlborough Wine requires wines to be made entirely from sustainably grown Marlborough grapes and bottled in New Zealand.

notes: Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is what New Zealand is best known for, with green, gooseberry, citrus and passion fruit notes.
Its Pinot Noir is aromatic, with red cherry fruit, fresh acidity and firm tannin for aging.
Chardonnay here leans to citrus, peach and melon.

blurb.text: New Zealand's largest wine region, in the north-east of the South Island, with about three quarters of national production and most of its exports. Sauvignon Blanc covers about 82% of the vines, and its wines are called some of the best of that style in the world. Pinot Noir is a distant second, and vineyards cluster around Blenheim and Seddon.
